full_judgment:
2. Facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of this Rule, are that opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 74 of 2000 on 19-4-2000 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur for a decree of partition of 0.50 acre land claiming saham of 0.1250 acre land in her favour. The case of the plaintiff in short is that 0.50 acre land belonged to Salim Jamaddar and after his death his four sons namely, Yeasin Jamaddar, Abdul Khaleque Jamaddar, Ismail Jamaddar, Habibur Rahman and three daughters, Shamsunnessa, Badrunnessa and Kamrunnessa inherited the land as per their respective shares. After death of Yeasin Jamaddar, his six sons namely, Mutahar, Moazzem, Enayet, Altaf, Mozaffar, three daughters, Badrunnessa, Zohra, Asiya and one wife Sakina inherited his share. Thereafter, RS Khatian No. 670 in respect of 0.50 acre land was prepared and finally published in the name of the heirs of Salim Jamaddar and Yeasin Jamaddar. Each son of Salim Jamaddar inherited 0.09 acre land and each daughter inherited 0.0450 acre land. Badrunnessa and Kamrunnessa settled their share measuring 0.09 acre land to their brother Ismail Jamaddar and thereafter, Ismail Jamaddar settled his land by pattan dated 15-4-1946 in favour of his four sons namely Yousuf, Yeakub, Ali Akbar and Haider. Khaleque Jamaddar sold his share to Sultan Kazi and thereafter, he re-purchased the same. Ali Akbar and Haider died while they were minors leaving behind their father Ismail Jamaddar. In the aforesaid way, Ismail Jamaddar became owner of 0.17 acre land and thereafter, died leaving behind two sons Yousuf, Yeakub and five daughters namely Nurjahan, Ayesha, Rokia, Rabeya, Kulsum and one wife Fuljan. Habibur Rahman died leaving behind one son Mahbubur Rahman. In the aforesaid way, the heirs of Yeasin Jamaddar, Ismail Jamaddar and Habibur Rahman became owners of 0.50 acre land and thereafter, they transferred the same by registered sale deed No. 3250 dated 8-3-1967 in favour of Sultan Miah, Abdur Razzak Miah, Enaruddin and Aneruddin and handed over possession thereof to them. While Sultan, Abdur Razzak, Enaruddin and Aneruddin were owners in possession of 0.1250 acre land each, Sultan and Abdur Razzak jointly transferred 0.1250 acre land in favour of Taijuddin by registered sale No. 2587 deed dated 26-4-1972 and .1250 acre land in favour of the plaintiff by registered sale deed No. 3176 dated 8-3-1976. In the aforesaid way, the plaintiff becomes owner in possession of 0.1250 acre land and SA Khatian was prepared with some mistakes. The plaintiff applied for mutation of her name but the concerned Tahsildar refused to do so. Cause of action of the suit arose on 30-3-2000 when the plaintiff requested the defendants to make partition of the suit property but they refused and, as such, the plaintiff was constrained to institute the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1-2 jointly and defendant No. 3 separately filed written statements to contest the suit contending that the suit is not maintainable, barred by limitation and bad for defect of parties. The positive case of defendant Nos. 1-2 is that during RS operation 0.50 acre land of RS Plot No. 1500 and 0.61 acre land of RS Plot No. 1528 was jointly recorded in the name of Abdul Khaleque Jamaddar and others in RS Khatian No. 670 and on an amicable partition Mozaffar Hossain and others got 0.20 acre land of RS Plot No. 1500 and 0.20 acre land of Plot No. 1528 and while they were owning and possessing said 0.40 acre land settled the same to Amena Khatun by registered patta No. 1259 dated 21-2-1947 and handed over possession thereof to her and on the basis of the pattan and her possession total 0.40 acre land was prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun in separate SA Khatian No. 363. Yousuf Ali Jamaddar and others got 0.31 acre land including 0.08 acre land from suit Plot No. 1500 and said 0.31 acre land was recorded in the name of Yousuf Ali Jamaddar and others in separate SA Khatian No. 730. Moreover, while Kazi Sultan Ahmed and others were owning and possessing 0.22 acre land SA Khatian No. 729 was prepared and finally published in their name. While Amena Khatun was owning and possessing 0.40 acre land transferred the same to Abul Fazal Khan @ Ali Miah by registered sale deed No. 3257 dated 4-7-1962 and handed over possession thereof to him who transferred the same to Sheikh Ramjan by registered sale deed No. 8289 dated 18-10-1976 and after mutating his name and paying rents thereof he transferred 0.20 acre land of suit Plot No. 1500 in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by registered sale deed No. 5498 dated 20-10-1986 and handed over possession thereof to them and they have been owning and possessing the same by payment of rent upon separation of the holding by mutation case. Accordingly, the RS recorded tenants lost their title to .20 acre land out of 0.50 acre land. 

 9. Mr Sk. Reajul Hogue learned Advocate appearing with Ms. Shishirkona, learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the Court of appeal, upon misreading and non-consideration of the evidence and misconception of law illegally allotted 0.1250 acre land in the saham of the plaintiff though her vendors had transferable right of 0.0250 acre land and in doing so did not discuss any evidence of the parties. Learned Advocate further submits that as the last court of facts, the Court of appeal did not evaluate or discuss any evidence independently and come to independent findings of fact or reversed the findings of fact of the trial Court but illegally reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Learned Advocate further submits that the Court of appeal erroneously held that complicated question of title is involved in the suit and a simple suit for partition is not maintainable but it decided the suit on merit and decreed the suit. Learned Advocate further submits that upon amicable partition among the RS recorded tenants, Mozaffar and others got 0.20 acre land out of 0.50 acre suit land and transferred the same to Amena Khatun by registered deed of pattan dated 21-2-1947 being No. 1259 and on the strength of said pattan separate SA Khatian No. 363 was prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun and accordingly, the said pattan has been acted upon and title of 0.20 acre land vested to Amena Khatun, who thereafter, transferred the same to Abul Fazal Kha vide registered sale date dated 4-7-1962 and accordingly, the RS recorded tenants and their successors lost their title to 0.20 acre land. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant Nos. 1-2 acquired title to 0.20 acre land through Amena Khatun by successive transfers through valid registered sale deeds and mutated their names in respect of 0.20 acre land and have been owning and possessing the same for more than 12 years and accordingly, they have acquired adverse possession in respect of said 0.20 acre land. Learned Advocate further submits that by deed No. 3250 dated 8-3-1967 though 0.50 acre land was shown to have been transferred to Sultan, Abdur Razzak, Enaruddinn and Aneruddin but the vendors of said deed had title to and transferable right of only 0.30 acre land and after deduction of 0.20 acre land, Sultan and three others acquired title to 0.0750 acre land each instead of 0.1250 acre land each. Learned Advocate further submits that after transfer of 0.1250 acre land to Taijuddin by Sultan and Razzak by registered sale deed dated 26-4-1972 they had title to only 0.0250 acre instead of 0.1250 acre land and accordingly, the plaintiff got title to only 0.0250 acre land from Sultan and Abdur Razzak by sale deed No. 3176 dated 8-3-1976. Learned Advocate further submits that the trial Court upon evaluation of evidence of the parties came to the conclusion that the plaintiff is entitled to 0.0250 acre land but the Court of appeal without discussing any evidence of the defendant Nos. 1-2 illegally reduced their share to 0.3525 acre from 0.4525 acre land and illegally increased share of the plaintiff from 0.0250 acre land to 0.1250 acre land. Learned Advocate finally submits that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal and, as such, liable to be set-aside. 

 11. As against the above contention, Mr Goutam Kumar Roy learned Advocate appearing for opposite party No. 1 submits that the Court of appeal, as the last Court of facts, upon considering the evidence and materials on record, rightly held that the plaintiff is entitled to 0.1250 acre land on the basis of sale deed dated 8-3-1976 and such findings of fact cannot be reversed in revisional jurisdiction. Learned Advocate further submits that the Court of appeal rightly held that the defendant could not prove pattan dated 21-2-1947 being No. 1255 and accordingly, they could not prove Amena's title to 0.20 acre land and since Amena Khatun could not acquire title to 0.20 acre land the defendants could not acquire title to said 0.20 acre land through Amena. Learned Advocate further submits that the Court of appeal upon considering the evidence held that Sultan Miah, Abdur Razzak, Enaruddin and Aneruddin acquired title to 0.50 acre land by registered sale deed dated 8-3-1967 from the heirs of Ismail and others and accordingly, the vendees of said deed acquired title to 0.50 acre land, in particular, Sultan and Razzak acquired title to 0.25 acre land jointly and after transfer of 0.1250 acre land to Taijuddin they had title to 0.1250 acre land which has been rightly transferred to the plaintiff by registered sale deed dated 8-3-1976 and, as such, the plaintiff has acquired title to said land not only by purchase but by adverse possession by owning and possessing the same by erecting dwelling hurts therein for more than 12 years. Learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff paid rent to the Government as well as paid municipal taxes in respect of 0.1250 acre land and it is settled principle of law that rent receipts are evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title. Learned Advocate further submits that the trial Court, upon misreading and non-consideration of evidence of the parties illegally allotted 0.0250 acre land in the saham of the plaintiff and, as such, the Court of appeal committed no error of law in allotting 0.1250 acre land in the saham of the plaintiff by modifying the judgment of the trial Court. 

 15. The plaintiff in her plaint as well as deposition of PW 1 stated that Salim Jamaddar was owner of 0.50 acre land and after his death his four sons namely Abdul Khaleque and others got 0.09 acre land each and three daughters namely Badrunnessa and others got 0.0450 acre land each and thereafter, Badrun-nessa and Kamarunnessa transferred their 0.09 acre land in favour of their brother Ismail who settled the same to his four sons Yusuf and others and thereafter, his two sons who were minors died leaving behind their father Ismail and accordingly, Ismail acquired title to 0.17 acre land and on the other hand Abdul Khaleque sold his share to Sultan Kazi and thereafter, he re-purchased said 0.09 acre land. Further case of the plaintiff that the heirs. of Yeasin, Habibur Rahman and Ismail acquired title to 0.50 acre land on amicable partition among the recorded tenants and their co-sharers and thereafter, they 'transferred the same to Sultan, Abdur Razzak, Enaruddin and Aneruddin by registered sale deed dated 9-3-1967 being No. 3250. The plaintiff produced the certified copy of said deed of sale dated 9-3-1967 which was marked as Exhibit No. 4. The plaintiff did not produce any deed of so-called pattan by which Badrunnessa and Kamarunnessa transferred 0.09 acre land in favour of Ismail and any deed of pattan by which Ismail transferred the same to his four sons. Accordingly, title of 0.09 acre land by Ismail from Badrunnessa and Kamarunnessa and by Yusuf and his three brothers from Ismail has not been established. 

 16. Against the above contention of the plaintiffs the defendants claimed that on an amicable partition among the RS recorded tenants and some of their heirs, Mozaffar and five others ( four sons and one daughter of Yeasin) got 0.20 acre land from the suit plot and other co-sharers got rest land with other land of other khatian and then Mozaffar and five others sold the same vide registered pattan No. 1259 dated 21-2-1947 to Amena Khatun and while she was owning and possessing the same separate SA Khatian was prepared and finally published in her name. The defendant also contended that after such transfer the rest RS recorded tenants and their successors had only transferable right and title to 0.30 acre land and accordingly, by sale deed dated 8-3-1967 Sultan and his three brothers acquired title to 0.0750 acre land each. Defendant Nos. 1-2 claimed title to said 0.20 acre land through successive transfers from Amena Khatun by sale deeds. In support of the transfer of 0.20 acre land in favour of Amena Khatun by Mozaffar and five others defendants Nos. 1-2 produced original copy of pattan dated 21-2-1947 and its related Index from the Sub-registry Office which were marked as Exhibit Nos. Ka and Ka(1)1 without any objection from the plaintiff. The plaintiff and defendant Nos. 1-2 produced certified copy SA Khatian No. 363 showing preparation and publication of 0.20 acre land in the name of Amena Khatun which was marked as Exhibit 1-Ga. Defendant Nos. 1-2 also produced rent receipts in the name of Amena Khatun in respect of 0.20 acre land which was marked as Exhibit No. Kha(3). They further contended that Amena Khatun transferred 0.20 acre land by registered sale deed dated 4-7-1962 to Abul Fazal Kha who transferred it to Sheikh Ramjan by sale deed No. 8289 dated 18-10-1976 who mutated his name and paid rents to the Government and thereafter, he transferred said 0.20 acre land to defendant Nos. 1-2 by registered sale deed No. 5498 dated 20-10-1986. They produced original copy of sale deed No. 3257 dated 4-7-1962, marked as Exhibit-Ja; certified copy of sale deed No. 8289 dated 18-10-1976, marked as Exhibit-Jha; rent receipts showing payment of rent by Ramjan marked as Exhibit Nos. Kha(4)-Kha(5); original sale deed No. 5498 dated 20-10-1986 marked as Exhibit-Ja(1). The defendants also produced rent receipts in the name of defendant Nos. 1-2 showing payment of rent of the suit land by them, marked as Exhibit Nos. Kha(6)-Kha(9). All those documents were marked as exhibits without any objection from the plaintiff. 

 17. While deposing as PW 1 the husband of the plaintiff namely, Muhammad Lalon Fakir stated, "এস, এ ৩৬৩নং খতিয়ানে আমিনা খাতুনের নামে ১৫০০ দাগে ২০ শতাংশ রেকর্ড হয়েছে কি না জানি না।" He further stated in cross-examination "সুলতান মিয়া, আব্দুর রাজ্জাক, এনার উদ্দিন ও আনার উদ্দিন এস, এ রেকর্ডের পরে জমি কিনে। এদের খরিদের আগেই আমিনা খাতুন ২০ শতাংশ কিনে এবং তার নামে এস, এ রেকর্ড হয়।" From the testimony of P.W 1, it is clear that Amena Khatun took settlement of 0.20 acre land and SA khatian was prepared and finally published in her name and thereafter, Sultan, Razzak, Enaruddin and Anaruddin purchased land. Considering above admission of the P.W1 as well as other evidence, the trial Court observed that by registered pattan No. 1259 dated 21-2-1947 [(Pattan Exhibit No. Ka and Index Exhibit No. Ka(1)] some of the RS recorded tenants and their successors transferred 0.20 acre land in favour of Amena Khatun by that pattan she acquired title to 0.20 acre land and SA khatian No. 363 (Exhibit No. Ga=1) was rightly prepared and finally published in her name and she paid rent to the Government [Exhibit (Kha(3)], who transferred the same to Abul Fazal Kha vide registered deed of sale No. 3257 dated 4-7-1962 (Exhibit Ja) who transferred the same to Sheikh Ramzan vide registered deed of sale No. 8289 dated 18-10-1976 (Exhibit Jha) and upon mutating his name he paid rent to the Government [Exhibit Nos. Kha (4) and Kha(5)] and thereafter, he transferred the same to defendant Nos. 1-2 vide registered deed of sale No. 5498 dared 20-10-1986 [Exhibit ja(1)] and upon mutating their names they paid rents to the Government [Exhibit Nos. Kha (6) and Kha(9)]. On relying upon those documentary evidence the trial Court came to the conclusion that after transfer of 0.20 acre land by RS recorded tenants and their successors they had title to remaining 0.30 acre land and accordingly, by sale deed No. 3250 dated 8-3- 1967 (Exhibit No. 4 = Jha(1)] Sultan, Razzak, Enaruddin and Anaruddin acquired title to only 0.30 acre land. 

 18. The Court of appeal disbelieved the said pattan and index [(Exhibits-Kha and Kha(1)] on the ground that those could not be read out as those were illegible and, as such, Amena Khatun could not acquire title to 0.20 acre land. Except this finding the Court of appeal did not consider the SA Khatian No. 363 which has been prepared and finally published on the basis of said pattan in the name of Amena Khatun and did not consider the transfer deeds dated 4-7-1962, 18-10-1976 and 20-10-1986 by which Amena Khatun transferred 0.20 acre land to Fazal Miah, who transferred the same to Sheikh Ramjan and thereafter, Ramjan Sheikh transferred said 0.20 acre land to defendant Nos. 1-2. The Court of appeal did not consider the rent receipts [(Exhibits Nos. Kha(3)-Kha(9)] by which Amena Khatun, Sheikh Ramjan and defendant Nos. 1-2 paid rents to the Government. 

 23. In the case of Erfan Ali vs Joynal Abedin Mia 35 DLR (AD) 216 it has been held that rent receipts are evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title. Section 110 of the Evidence Act provides a presumption of ownership in favour of person who is in possession of the property and possession follows title. Moreover, as per section 144A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, every entry in a record of rights prepared or revised under section 144 shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. By producing SA Khatian No. 363 (Exhibit-Ga) defendant Nos. 1-2 contended that the SA Khatian was rightly prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun on the basis of pattan dated 21-2-1947 (Exhibit-Ka). Though the plaintiff claimed that said deed of pattan was a product of forgery and the SA record was wrongly prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun but she could not rebut the presumption of correctness of the SA Khatian by adducing any reliable evidence. Accordingly, it is to be presumed that deed of pattan dated 21-2-1947 has been acted upon and SA Khatian No. 363 was rightly prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun. Though the plaintiff claimed that the title deeds by which defendant Nos. 1 and 2 claimed title to the suit land were forged documents but the original sale deeds were produced by the defendants and those were marked as exhibits without any objection from the plaintiff. Accordingly, it is to be presumed that those sale deeds are genuine documents. The defendants by producing oral and documentary evidence have been able to prove that they have been owning and possessing 0.4525 acre land for more than 12 years through their predecessors before filing of the suit and, as such, they have acquired title to and possession of 0.4525 acre land by way of adverse possession.
